Based on the retrieved excerpts, the following ISO 45001 clauses are in play for your situation:

## **Clause 5.4 — Consultation and participation of workers**

This clause directly supports involving your tower crews in selecting replacement harnesses. It requires the organization to establish processes for **consultation and participation of workers** in the **development, planning, implementation** and **improvement actions** of the OH&S system, with **special emphasis on the involvement of non-managerial workers**. Your tower crews (non-managerial workers) should be actively engaged in selecting equipment that affects their safety and comfort.

## **Clause 8.1.2 — Hierarchy of controls**

This clause is critical because it reveals that **relying on personal protective equipment (PPE) is the last resort** in the hierarchy. The fact that crews are loosening their harnesses indicates a potential failure in this control measure. The clause requires processes to **eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks** by first attempting to **eliminate the hazard**, then **substitute**, then apply **engineering controls and work reorganization**, then **administrative controls**, and only lastly PPE. You should evaluate whether fall risks can be addressed higher in the hierarchy rather than solely depending on harnesses.

## **Clause 7.3 — Awareness**

This clause requires workers to be made aware of **hazards and risks that concern them** and **the implications of not conforming**. Crews loosening harnesses suggests they may not fully understand the serious consequences, or the equipment genuinely impedes safe work. Their feedback about discomfort should inform both awareness efforts and equipment selection.

## **Clause 10.2 — Incident and nonconformity response**

The practice of loosening harnesses constitutes a **nonconformity** with safety requirements. This clause requires you to **evaluate — with participation of workers** — the need for corrective action, **review existing OH&S risk assessments**, and **determine and implement corrective actions in line with the hierarchy of controls**. Involving crews in harness selection aligns with the required worker participation in corrective action evaluation.

---

**Summary:** The core driver is **5.4** (worker participation), supported by **8.1.2** (questioning reliance on PPE), **7.3** (ensuring awareness), and **10.2** (corrective action for the nonconformity of loosened harnesses).
